# John Meredith

## Overview

- **Age:** Younger than 50  <sub>[v5 c2 P21](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0021), [v5 c4 P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v5 c1 P12](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0012)</sub>
- **Status:** Engaged to be married  <sub>[v5 c34 P38](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0038), [v5 c35 P0](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0000)</sub>
- **Rank:** Presbyterian Minister  <sub>[v5 c1 P12](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0012), [v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008)</sub>
- **Origin:** Maywater  <sub>[v5 c4 P48](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0048)</sub>
- **Role:** Minister of Glen St. Mary Presbyterian Church  <sub>[v5 c1 P12](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0012), [v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007), [v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008)</sub>
- **Titles:** Reverend  <sub>[v5 c1 P12](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0012)</sub>; Mr. Meredith  <sub>[v5 c1 P12](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0012)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Jack  <sub>[v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a very comely man with ivory-like, clear-cut features and slender hands, though he often presents an unkempt appearance with unbrushed hair, faded dressing gown, and slippers. He has dark, dreamy, fine eyes, a high brow, a strong, clean-shaven chin, and a mouth that indicates a capacity for understanding. He is stoop-shouldered, has absurdly long legs, and possesses a remarkably strong grip.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P6](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0006), [v5 c2 P12](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0012), [v5 c2 P15](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0015), [v5 c6 P2](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0002), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P10](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0010), [v5 c14 P20](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0020), [v5 c21 P12](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0012)_

## Personality

He is a deeply spiritual, learned, and eloquent preacher, but lacks practical common sense and is exceptionally absent-minded and moony. Though shy and aloof on the surface, he possesses the heart of a boy and a gentle, humble, and forgiving nature. He lives largely in a world of books and abstractions, often getting so absorbed in his reading or meditations that he forgets his meals and duties. He loves his children dearly, but struggles to manage them without a wife, ruling his home solely through love rather than sternness.

_Sources: [v5 c2 P7](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0007), [v5 c2 P8](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0008), [v5 c2 P11](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0011), [v5 c4 P1](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0001), [v5 c4 P2](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0002), [v5 c9 P5](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0005), [v5 c13 P2](../source/v05-c13.md#nw-v05-c13-p0002), [v5 c14 P21](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0021), [v5 c14 P29](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0029), [v5 c14 P39](../source/v05-c14.md#nw-v05-c14-p0039), [v5 c21 P2](../source/v05-c21.md#nw-v05-c21-p0002)_

## History

After the death of his beloved wife, Cecilia, John Meredith was left alone to raise their four young children with the assistance of his elderly, half-blind relative, Aunt Martha. Moving from Maywater to Glen St. Mary, he accepted the call to become the minister of the Presbyterian church, winning the congregation over with his brilliant preaching despite his extreme absent-mindedness and the undisciplined antics of his motherless children. During his time at Glen St. Mary, he frequently lost himself in theological studies, forgetting meals, church announcements, and various pastoral duties. His children formed a 'Good-Conduct Club' to discipline themselves after public criticism of their behavior, leading to an incident where his daughter Una fainted from fasting, deeply shocking him into a realization of his parental shortcomings. Shortly after, Mrs. Alec Davis attempted to adopt Una, which he fiercely refused, declaring his love for his children. Over time, he developed deep feelings for Rosemary West, whom he met by a spring in Rainbow Valley, but when he proposed to her she rejected him by letter due to a secret vow she had made to her sister. Despairing of his love, he remained devoted to his family until Una, discovering his heartache and learning the truth from Rosemary, intervened to reconcile them. Re-assured of her affection, Mr. Meredith met Rosemary again at the spring, where she accepted his proposal, leading to their planned autumn marriage.
